newsitem.title: TURKEY: Nine Istanbul casinos closed after ban on Turks.
newsitem.headline: Nine Istanbul casinos closed after ban on Turks.

text.p: Istanbul's governor temporarily closed nine five-star hotel casinos in the city after police found they contravened a ban by the Islamist-led government on Turkish customers, a police spokesman said on Thursday.
"They were closed for three days from Wednesday night, because they broke the ban," he told Reuters.

The government last month ordered that Turks be excluded from casinos, saying that families were broken up by gambling. There were also wide concerns that the gambling industry is used for money laundering.

The spokesman said the casino directors will have to pay a fine of just under one dollar if they are convicted under article 526 of Turkish penal code, which punishes disobedience to the government's orders.
The interior ministry warned all provincial governers of the country last week to demand stricter identity checks at casinos to ensure Turks are kept out.
Leading figures in the casino industry, which depends primarily on domestic gamblers, have protested against the ban.
